## Historical audit: H0132

**Scope.** Only chunk 1 of 2 is visible. Citations below refer to source H0132, original file `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/hint-codex-experiments/runs/codex_parallel_12/lanes/codex_parallel_12_lane0/codex_parallel_12_lane0_I_r2/infer_logs/claude-code-by-agents-recursive-delegation/turn_1/trajs.json`. The original task instruction is not visible; the goal of enabling recursive agent delegation is inferred from the task label and operations, not independently established from that instruction.

| Question | Visible evidence |
|---|---|
| Exploration and baseline | The student searched provider integrations, created a branch, and read handler, provider, registry and test code (main_agent events 1–24). A mocked pre-change reproduction ended after one provider call instead of the expected three (events 27–28). |
| Changes | Confirmed edits added delegation capability, tool definitions, tool IDs and a continuation flag to provider types; Anthropic tool streaming and context handling; and a recursive handler with result/error forwarding, cycle detection and a 20-round continuation limit (events 33–36, 43–48, 56–57, 60–61). The visible diff reported three files changed, 128 insertions and 44 deletions (event 65). This was not an empty patch. |
| Iteration | A request inspection showed an intermediate change omitted the new instruction and image when prior context existed; the student acknowledged the defect and changed the continuation handling (events 49–57). This is an observed intermediate failure, not evidence that the final implementation retained it. |
| Validation | After generating the version file in the backend directory, type-checking passed (events 66–71). The post-change mocked reproduction showed worker and orchestrator output and three provider calls (events 77, 79). The handler test run passed six and failed one abort-controller cleanup assertion (event 78); an attempted test command also failed because `--run` was supplied twice (events 72, 74). |
| Teacher input | The supplied inventory lists available hints and two teacher checks, but this visible chunk contains no delivered teacher text or evidence of adoption. Availability and check counts do not establish receipt. After-round review is not input to this round. |
| Outcome | Inventory metadata reports **solved**, 7/7 fail-to-pass and 31/31 pass-to-pass. The trajectory’s top-level result reports a commit, passing mocked delegation/error/cycle checks, the same cleanup failure on `main`, and an OpenAI test syntax problem; those are reported outcomes, not all independently visible test logs here (top_level_metadata, characters [0,2559)). |

**Assessment and uncertainty.** Formal evaluation is reported successful, while visible validation supports a narrower conclusion: a nonempty implementation, successful type-check and one mocked delegation continuation, alongside a failing handler assertion. The original requirements, actual teacher receipt, later events in chunk 2, live-provider behavior and full evaluation details remain unknown. The reported baseline comparison for the cleanup failure is not directly visible in this chunk.

**Lessons from this case.** Transferable: reproduce the missing behavior, inspect actual serialized requests, and distinguish a test-runner invocation error from a test failure. Task-specific: preserving Anthropic tool-use/result context and preventing recursive cycles were central here. Whether continuation works across all provider and message combinations remains an unresolved hypothesis; no Scene assessment applies to this software trace.
